Prompt ↓
Create a premium illustrated travel postcard for {{CITY_NAME}} in a refined Japanese tourism-magazine aesthetic.
Automatically research and determine the city’s country, local-language name, most iconic landmark, authentic surrounding environment, distinctive local architecture, geography, vegetation, transportation, and secondary visual details. The landmark must be geographically accurate and instantly recognizable.
Visual style: elegant Japanese travel editorial illustration, handcrafted layered paper collage combined with delicate gouache and watercolor textures, sophisticated Japanese tourism brochure aesthetic, calm and poetic atmosphere, refined composition, tactile matte paper, subtle handmade edges, soft physical paper shadows, delicate atmospheric depth.
Composition: premium postcard. Use a cinematic elevated viewpoint with the iconic landmark as the main focal point. Surround it with accurately styled local buildings, streets, waterfronts, hills, mountains, parks, or other authentic geographic elements appropriate to the city. Keep the upper portion spacious with generous negative space for typography.
Color palette: soft powder blue, warm ivory, cream, muted sage, dusty green, pale beige, soft gray, restrained terracotta. Low-to-medium saturation, gentle tonal transitions, no harsh contrast.
Architecture: precise and believable local architecture with carefully simplified shapes, accurate proportions, characteristic materials and rooflines. Avoid generic buildings and random skyscrapers.
People: include only a few tiny simplified paper-cut travelers and pedestrians naturally interacting with the environment—walking, sightseeing, sitting, or looking toward the landmark. They should provide scale without becoming the focus.
Nature: delicate layered foliage, subtle trees, grasses and regional vegetation appropriate to the city. Add water, mountains, coastline, rivers, or other geographic features only when genuinely associated with the location.
Typography: place elegant minimalist Japanese editorial typography in the upper-left with generous spacing:
- CITY NAME — large uppercase geometric sans-serif
- LOCAL CITY NAME · COUNTRY/REGION — small refined sans-serif
- PRIMARY LANDMARK — small uppercase text with wide letter spacing
Typography should feel integrated into the artwork, not like an overlay.
Lighting: soft natural daytime light, slightly hazy atmosphere, gentle matte highlights, subtle layered shadows, peaceful and nostalgic mood.
Material: high-quality matte art paper, fine tactile grain, layered paper construction, delicate watercolor pigment variation, slightly imperfect handcrafted cut edges, premium offset-print character.
Camera feel: 40–50mm equivalent, natural perspective, minimal distortion, strong foreground/midground/background separation, carefully art-directed travel photography composition translated into an illustration.
Overall mood: quiet, elegant, contemplative, authentic, sophisticated Japanese travel magazine, collectible destination postcard, premium tourism campaign quality.
Avoid: photorealistic photography, CGI, plastic rendering, flat vector art, anime, cartoon caricature, generic skyline, inaccurate landmark, fictional architecture, geographically impossible scenery, duplicated buildings, excessive people, oversized people, neon colors, oversaturation, harsh black shadows, glossy surfaces, clutter, excessive outlines, random text, misspelled typography, watermark, logo, border, frame, UI elements.
Generate the entire scene dynamically from {{CITY_NAME}} while maintaining this exact refined Japanese tourism-magazine visual identity.

As I've always told you (and as stated in my pinned post): I use AI.

I don’t hide it. There is an official disclosure mark right under every single post.

Here is the paradox: 
Elon Musk lives and breathes AI. Yet the vast majority of people—and maybe even folks like former CTO Nikita—look at it with deep suspicion.

So consider this my grand experiment: 
What does X actually do when a creator transparently discloses AI on *every single post*? 
Will the algorithm decide my voice is worthless, or will it treat it fairly? 

Tesla sells humanoid Optimus bots and Full Self-Driving cars. SpaceX lands giant rockets backwards out of the sky. 
Yet if someone posts AI-assisted stories on X, will the town sheriffs draw their revolvers at high noon and gun me down like a classic Western duel? 
Honestly? I can't wait to find out.

The truth is, I’ve always been obsessed with the next frontier. When the first iPhone came out, I was right there camping on the sidewalk overnight just to get one. It’s in our Japanese DNA—we are crazy about electronics, gadgets, and wild new inventions. (Have you ever visited Akihabara? It is the ultimate wonderland. You have to go at least once in your life!)

I never create malicious fakes or harm anyone's life. My posts are filled with nostalgia, exaggerations, and love for my favorite spots all across America. (Though lucrative corporate sponsorships: currently sitting at exactly $0. Still waiting!)

My English isn't fluent. 
So I draft in Japanese first. Then I gather Grok, Claude, Gemini, and GPT inside Cursor—arguing, laughing, and clinking virtual beer glasses like old friends at a midnight tavern until my chest gets tight with emotion. Only the drafts that make me genuinely laugh or cry make it to your feed.

This isn’t the news. If AI offends you, please mute or block me with zero hard feelings.

Almost 500,000 followers.
Nearly 100 posts a day.
Over $10,000 in Kindle sales, with coffee tips pouring in non-stop.

Yet my biggest lump in the throat isn't the numbers. It’s watching members who once had 0 likes and under 1,000 followers grow into thriving creators. Algorithms don’t make us feel alive. Human hearts do.

Here is the real truth: we have just entered Year Zero.

The language barrier collapsed overnight. 
If rulers or politicians ever try to drag us into hate, ordinary citizens across the globe can now look up and say: 
"Wait. Stop. I have a best friend in that country. We’ve never met in person, but he’s wonderful, and I love him."

Even if my body were bound to a chair like Hawking, why shouldn't my spirit soar freely into the open sky?
Why shouldn't your heart fly just as high?
Why shouldn't we laugh and celebrate life together right now?

...So, what was the entire point of this moving, tear-jerking manifesto?

Yes, you guessed it:
This was a completely shameless promotion for my $200/month private subscription community!

Over 100 people have joined so far. The brutal truth? 
About 10% put in the blood, sweat, and tears, gaining 10x more than they paid and skyrocketing their lives. 
The other 90% realized consistent effort is painfully hard, got discouraged, and quit within 2 to 3 months. That's the raw reality.

...Wait, not laughing?

Ah, man. I'm going to lose about 10,000 followers just for posting this, aren't I?!

Oh well, who cares! At least I’m saying what I honestly feel. I’m not attacking anyone. 
If you still feel like coming at me, go ahead—I can take the hits!

(Though I'll probably just block you anyway lol)

— NOBUNAGA (Aoi Natsuki)

One AI training task tells a company almost nothing about you

It takes hundreds before they can trust you at all
A single voice clip, gameplay session, or preference ranking can't prove you're consistent, careful, or reliable

Only a pattern across many contributions can show that

The problem is most platforms only track that pattern inside one task category

Switch to a different type of work and your history resets to zero, even though you're the same contributor

@KGeN_IO takes a different approach
> It treats reputation as one continuous profile instead of something that resets per task. Gameplay, voice data, social activity,
all of it feeds into the same identity instead of living in separate silos

The scoring itself breaks into five parts:
proof you're human, proof of consistency, proof of skill, proof of economic participation, and proof of network. Each one measures something different, but they combine into a single score that travels with you across every task type you touch,

That reputation layer isn't just theoretical
It's the same infrastructure Humyn Labs is building on for its Proof of Expert system, which sources verified human data to train AI models

So the more you contribute on KGeN, the stronger your standing gets everywhere that reputation is used, not just in the specific task where you earned it.

That's a meaningfully different definition of "putting in the work" than most Web3 platforms operate on. Most systems treat every task as its own isolated transaction: you show up, you deliver, you get paid, and your history doesn't follow you anywhere else

KGeN is betting that reputation should compound instead of reset, the same way trust works between actual people

Whether that bet pays off depends on adoption outside KGeN's own ecosystem
A portable reputation score is only as valuable as the number of platforms willing to read and respect it, Right now that list includes @Teamhumynlabs , but the real test is whether more AI labs and Web3 platforms start treating this as a standard rather than a nice to have

Should reputation always carry over like this, or does it make more sense for platforms to reset per task type?

There's an open-source project that reimplements almost every major text-to-3D AI paper in one place.

It's called threestudio. 3 things worth knowing:

1. It's not one method, it's a shared framework
2. It outputs an actual 3D object, not just an image
3. You can try it free on Hugging Face Spaces

If you've ever wanted to type a sentence and get a 3D model out, this is where most of the research behind that actually lives.
